body.statement: Using \(\mathrm{FRHandle}\), prove for every input \(\mathsf{Data}\) the equivalence \[\Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}<\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\text{a valid finite }\mathsf{GapCert}\text{ exists}.\] The certificate verifier must use exact polynomial reduction and sign determination on \(\mathbb A_{\mathrm{rep}}\), with outward-rounded rational arithmetic used only for objective enclosures. Let \(d\) be the total number of real variables in the two standard-form programs, \(B\) the binary input length, and \(\Delta=\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}-\Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}>0\). Establish an exact terminating construction by real-closed-field quantifier elimination with bit complexity at most \((B+\lceil\log_2(1/\Delta)\rceil+1)^{2^{O(d)}}\); interval refinement must terminate with \(\sup I_N<\inf I_D\). The result must include nonunique optimizers, zero donor weights, redundant predictor columns, and tight or collapsed Lorentz-cone blocks.
body.justification: Necessity plus a representation-dependent termination guarantee turns a sufficient check into a complete, reproducible frontier characterization.
body.gap: Pataki2013 gives facial-reduced strong duals and JeyakumarKumLee2008 characterizes closed-cone Farkas duality, but neither derives an iff strict support-value certificate or a separation-sensitive exact-arithmetic bound for these synthetic-control SOCPs.
body.consumer: The certificate lets \texttt{scpi} distinguish a genuine precision gain from solver tolerance or alternative optima on a lower-dimensional face.
